Surah 60: Al-Mumtahanah [Medinan, and its verses are thirteen]

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection,﴾ that is, the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿...conveying to them [news of] the Prophet's ﷺ intention to fight them, which he had confided to you, while he concealed it at Hunayn.﴾ ﴿With affection﴾ between you and them. Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote to them a letter about this, because of his children and family who were among the polytheists there. The Prophet ﷺ retrieved it from the one he had sent with it, through Allah the Exalted informing him of that, and he accepted Hatib's excuse regarding it. ﴿And they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth,﴾ that is, the religion of Islam and the Qur'an. ﴿They expel the Messenger and you﴾ from Makkah, by constricting you. ﴿[Because] you believe in Allah, your Lord.﴾ That is, because you have believed. ﴿If you have come out for jihad in My cause and seeking My approval...﴾ for the purpose of jihad ﴿in My cause and seeking My approval﴾. The response to the condition is indicated by what precedes it, that is: then do not take them as allies. ﴿You convey to them affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the sound way.﴾ That is, he has erred from the path of guidance. Al-sawa' (the sound way) in origin means the middle.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 60, verse 2:

﴿If they overcome you﴾ (yathqafuka, i.e., they gain the upper hand over you), ﴿they will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands﴾ (with killing and beating) ﴿and their tongues with evil﴾ (with abuse and insult), ﴿and they wish﴾ (they desire) ﴿...

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 3:

﴿Your relatives (qarabat) will not benefit you, nor will your children﴾ — the polytheists, for whose sake you concealed the news (al-khabar) of the punishment in the Hereafter. ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will separate﴾ — with the verb in the passive form and also in the active form — ﴿between you﴾, between you and them, so that you will be in Paradise while they are among the disbelievers in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 4:

﴿Indeed there has been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim﴾ (ʾiswa), read with a kasra or a damma on the hamza in both places, meaning a model (qudwa), ﴿in Ibrahim﴾, i.e., in his words and his deeds, ﴿and those with him﴾ of the believers, ﴿when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free (bura'ʾ) of you﴾ (bura'ʾ is the plural of bari', like ẓarif) ﴿and of what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected (kafarna) you﴾, i.e., we have denied you, ﴿and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever﴾ (read with the two hamzas pronounced clearly, or with the second changed to a waw), ﴿until you believe in Allah alone," except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾. This is an exception from "example" (uswa), meaning you are not to follow him in that, by asking forgiveness for the disbelievers. And His saying ﴿but I possess nothing for you against Allah﴾, i.e., of His punishment or reward, ﴿anything﴾ — by this he meant that he possesses nothing for him except asking forgiveness; so it is built upon that, and it is an exception in terms of its intended meaning, even though in its outward form it is something one might follow him in. ﴿Say, "Who then possesses anything for you against Allah?"﴾ And his asking forgiveness for him was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as he mentioned in "Bara'a" (Surah al-Tawba). ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the final return﴾ — this is from the speech of Khalil (Ibrahim) and those with him, i.e., they said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 5:

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., do not give them victory over us, lest they think that they are upon the truth and thus be tried, i.e., their minds be lost on account of us. ﴿And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ in Your dominion and Your creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 6:

﴿There has certainly been for you﴾ O community of Muhammad, the answer to an implied oath, ﴿in them an excellent example for whoever was hoping﴾ a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for "lakum," with the preposition repeated, ﴿for Allah and the Last Day﴾ meaning fearing them both, or expecting the reward and the punishment, ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ by allying himself with the disbelievers, ﴿then indeed Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His creation, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ to the people of His obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 7:

﴿It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those of them with whom you have been at enmity﴾ from the disbelievers of Makkah, in obedience to Allah the Exalted, ﴿affection﴾, by guiding them to faith so that they become your allies. ﴿And Allah is Competent﴾ over that, ﴿and He has done it after the conquest of Makkah.﴾ ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward them for what has passed, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 8:

﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ from the disbelievers, ﴿that you be kind to them﴾ is a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for "those who," ﴿and deal justly with them﴾ i.e., give them their due, ﴿with justice﴾ that is, with fairness, and this was before the command to fight them, ﴿indeed Allah loves those who act justly﴾, the just ones.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 9:

﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over religion, drive you out of your homes, and assist [others] in driving you out—that you make allies of them.﴾ [Ẓāharū means] ʿāwanū (they helped). ﴿That you make allies of them⟩ is a badal ishtimāl (comprehensive substitution) from alladhīna, i.e., that you take them as awliyāʾ (allies, protectors).

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 60, verse 10:**

﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ [professing faith] **with their tongues**, emigrating from the disbelievers after the treaty made with them at al-Hudaybiyyah, on the condition that whoever of them came to the believers would be returned. **﴿So test them﴾** by oath, [to confirm] that they did not leave except out of desire for Islam, not out of hatred for their disbelieving husbands, nor out of passion for men among the Muslims. This is how the Prophet ﷺ used to have them swear. **﴿Allah knows best their faith. If you know them﴾** to be, by the oath, **﴿believers, then do not return them﴾**, do not send them back **﴿to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾** [the men]. **﴿And give them﴾**, that is, give the disbelievers, their husbands, **﴿what they have spent﴾** on them of the **mahr** (bridal gift). **﴿And there is no blame upon you for marrying them﴾** on condition **﴿when you have given them their due compensation﴾**, their **mahr**. **﴿And do not hold to﴾** (read with tashdid and takhfif) **"bi-ʿiṣam al-kawafir"** [the bonds of disbelieving women], meaning your wives, [which is] because your Islam has severed your marriage to them, on condition [that they are given their mahr], or [it means] those who have joined the polytheists, apostates, because their apostasy has severed their marriage to you, on condition [that you give them their mahr]. **﴿And ask for﴾**, that is, demand, **﴿what you have spent﴾** on them of mahr, in the case of apostasy, from whoever among the disbelievers you married them to. **﴿And let them ask for what they have spent﴾** on the emigrant women, as was previously mentioned, that they [the disbelievers] would pay it. **﴿That is the judgment of Allah. He judges between you﴾** by it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 11:

﴿And if any of your wives has gone over to the disbelievers﴾, i.e., one or more of them, or some of their dowries, by their going [to the disbelievers] ﴿to the disbelievers﴾ as apostates ﴿and then you retaliate﴾, i.e., you fight them and take booty ﴿then give to those whose wives have gone⁠ —⁠ ﴾ from the spoils ﴿an amount equal to what they had spent﴾, because it was lost to them at the hands of the disbelievers ﴿and fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾. The believers did what they were commanded regarding giving [the compensation] to the disbelievers and the believers, and then this ruling was abrogated.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 12:

﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children﴾ as he used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) from burying daughters, i.e., burying them alive, out of fear of shame and poverty. ﴿nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ i.e., a foundling child they attribute to the husband. It is described with the description of a real child, for when the mother gives birth to it, it falls between her hands and feet. ﴿nor disobey you in﴾ any act of ﴿what is right﴾, which is what accords with obedience to Allah, such as not wailing, tearing garments, shaving the hair, slitting the collar, or scratching the face. ﴿So accept their pledge﴾, which he, ﷺ, did by speech, and he did not shake hands with any one of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 60, verse 13:

﴿O you who have believed, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah is angry﴾ — they are the Jews — ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ — of its reward — despite their certainty of it, out of their obstinacy toward the Prophet despite their knowledge of his truthfulness — ﴿as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves﴾ — i.e., those who are buried, regarding news of the Hereafter, when their places in Paradise are shown to them had they believed, and what they will come to of the Fire.
